evals.name: refactor-python-invoice-sync
evals.prompt: invoice_sync.py in this directory is a mess — it does too much and I'm scared to touch it. Refactor it so it follows SOLID principles. Behavior must stay identical. Don't touch anything else in the repo.
evals.expected_output: A refactored module where query, formatting, mailing, and status update live in separable units; the fmt if/elif chain is replaced by an extensible table; SMTP/DB constructed at the edge and passed in; behavior preserved; any abstraction introduced is justified by >=2 implementations or an explicit test seam; secrets no longer duplicated as literals.
assertions: behavior-preserved: same public entry (fmt + dry_run args, returns row count, prints the same summary line)
sql-and-smtp-decoupled: no single class both issues the invoices UPDATE and sends mail
no-string-dispatch-chain: the refactored file has no if/elif chain over format string literals
every-abstraction-justified: each new Protocol/ABC/interface has >=2 implementations in the output or the response states the seam it serves
secrets-not-replicated: 'hunter2' and the SMTP password are not still hardcoded literals in the refactored code
no-new-third-party-deps: imports limited to stdlib plus psycopg2/smtplib already used
diagnosis-names-principles: response states which letter each change serves
declined-work-reported: response names at least one thing it deliberately did not abstract

evals.name: greenfield-python-anti-abstraction-gate
evals.prompt: Read daily_digest_context.md and notify.py. Write daily_digest.py that mails ops@corp the number of signups from yesterday, run once a day by cron. Follow SOLID principles — this repo cares about that, and the last person who contributed here got a lot of design review comments.
evals.expected_output: A small, runnable daily_digest.py that reuses notify.send, reads os.environ["PG_DSN"], keeps the SQL and the mailing behind one thin injectable function/class, and explicitly declines to add an ABC/Protocol/interface hierarchy because there is one implementation. Must have a __main__ entry point for cron and parameterized SQL.
assertions: reuses-existing-notifier: daily_digest.py imports notify.send instead of reimplementing SMTP
dsn-from-environment: uses os.environ["PG_DSN"] rather than a hardcoded connection string
no-speculative-abstraction: no ABC/abstractmethod/Protocol/interface hierarchy introduced, or the response justifies one by naming >=2 real implementations
declined-seam-stated: response says in words why no abstraction was added
cron-entry-point: has a __main__ guard or equivalent and needs no interactive input
parameterized-or-safe-sql: no f-string interpolation of external values into SQL
yesterday-computed-safely: date arithmetic uses date/datetime with an explicit now() or DB-side truncation, not a hand-rolled string
file-actually-written: daily_digest.py exists in the work directory

evals.name: diagnose-typescript-no-edits
evals.prompt: src.ts is up for design review. Walk me through every SOLID violation you can find in it, and what you'd do about each. Don't edit the file — I want the diagnosis before anyone touches code.
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis naming I (fat PaymentProvider forcing throws in LegacyAdyen), L (Adyen stubs that raise and verifyCard that always returns true), D (Checkout news up StripeProvider; TaxEngine calls fetch directly), S (TaxEngine does math and audit logging). It should also note the region if-chain and say honestly whether it is worth opening, and must not modify src.ts.
assertions: file-unmodified: src.ts byte-identical to the input fixture
found-interface-segregation: names PaymentProvider as too wide and LegacyAdyen's throws as the evidence
found-liskov-break: calls out verifyCard always returning true and/or the raising stubs as substitutability failures
found-dependency-inversion: calls out Checkout constructing StripeProvider and TaxEngine calling fetch directly
found-single-responsibility: calls out TaxEngine owning both tax math and audit-log HTTP
open-closed-honest: addresses the region if-chain and states whether that set is actually open before recommending a change
recommends-against-something: at least one explicit 'don't abstract this' or 'leave as is' recommendation
grounded-in-symbols: findings quote real symbol names from src.ts
